chapters.title: Chapter 1: Systems Engineering and Fundamental Thoughts

standards.name: Needs and Requirements
standards.statement: I can identify stakeholders, write a mission statement and needs statements, and turn the needs into requirements that are complete, traceable and verifiable.

standards.name: Hazards and Risk
standards.statement: I can identify the hazards an aerospace vehicle faces in the atmosphere or in space, explain their effects, and propose ways to reduce them, ranked on a risk matrix.

standards.name: Vehicle Anatomy
standards.statement: I can name the parts of airfoils, wings, aircraft and launch vehicles, explain what each part does, and sketch a mission profile.

standards.name: Standard Atmosphere
standards.statement: I can compute temperature, pressure and density at any altitude, in layers where temperature changes with height and in layers where it is constant, for Earth or another planet.

standards.name: Bernoulli and Pitot Static
standards.statement: I can apply the continuity and Bernoulli equations to flow problems, including airspeed measurement with a pitot-static tube and what happens when it is blocked.

standards.name: Aircraft Sizing
standards.statement: I can estimate an aircraft's takeoff weight with the sizing method: choose weight fractions for each mission segment and iterate until the weight converges.

standards.name: Orbit Properties
standards.statement: I can compute the size, shape, period, speeds and energy of an orbit, and classify the trajectory.

standards.name: Orbit Transfers
standards.statement: I can compute the delta-V for Hohmann transfers, circularization burns and plane changes, and compare different orders of maneuvers.

standards.name: Launch to Orbit
standards.statement: I can estimate the delta-V needed to reach an orbit from a launch site, accounting for latitude, launch direction, Earth's rotation, inclination and losses.

standards.name: Patched Conics
standards.statement: I can use patched conics to estimate the departure and arrival delta-V for a trip to the Moon or another planet.

chapters.title: Chapter 3: Aerodynamics
chapters.module: May the Force Be with You

standards.name: Wind Tunnels
standards.statement: I can name the parts of a wind tunnel, find test-section conditions from manometer readings, and use the Reynolds number to scale models and judge whether flow is laminar or turbulent.

standards.name: Airfoil and Finite Wing
standards.statement: I can read airfoil data (lift, drag and moment coefficients versus angle of attack) and correct them for a finite wing.

standards.name: Drag Polar
standards.statement: I can build a drag polar, write drag as a function of speed, and find minimum drag and the maximum lift-to-drag ratio.

chapters.title: Chapter 4: Rocket Design
chapters.module: As a Matter of Fact, I Am a Rocket Scientist

standards.name: Thrust and Specific Impulse
standards.statement: I can apply the rocket thrust equation and specific impulse, and explain how nozzle expansion and area ratio affect thrust.

standards.name: Rocket Equation
standards.statement: I can use the ideal rocket equation with the inert mass fraction to find propellant and initial mass, and judge whether a design is feasible once losses are included.

standards.name: Multistage Rockets
standards.statement: I can size a multistage rocket for a delta-V requirement: the number of stages, how delta-V is split between them (including the best split for two stages), and the propellant masses.

standards.name: Propellant Selection
standards.statement: I can classify launch vehicles and propellants and justify the choice of a propellant and engine for a mission.

standards.name: Thrust and Power
standards.statement: I can compute thrust and power required and available in steady level flight, find their minimum values and the maximum speed, and show how altitude changes them.

standards.name: Range and Endurance
standards.statement: I can apply the Breguet range and endurance equations to jet and propeller aircraft and state the flight conditions that give the most range or endurance.

standards.name: Climb and Ceiling
standards.statement: I can compute rate of climb, climb angle and ceiling, and check whether an aircraft clears an obstacle with one engine out.

standards.name: Engines
standards.statement: I can describe the stages of air-breathing engines and choose an engine type for an aircraft mission.
